papers.paper_title: EXAMINATION PAPER 1: II SEMESTER MGU UGP25 - MARCH - 2025

questions.question: What is the meaning of management?
questions.solution_html:
• Management refers to the process of planning, organizing, leading, and controlling resources—such
  • as people, finances, materials, or information—to achieve specific goals efficiently and effectively.
  • It's about coordinating efforts, making decisions, and guiding actions to ensure that objectives are met
  • while balancing productivity, innovation, and sustainability.
  • Empowerment of Lower Levels: Authority to make decisions is delegated to
  • managers, departments, or teams closer to the actual work or customer interactions.
  • This allows decisions to be more relevant to specific situations.
  • Setting Objectives: Define clear and measurable goals that the organization aims to
  • achieve.
  • Time-Consuming: Planning requires significant time and effort, which might delay
  • immediate actions.
  • Provides Direction: It sets clear objectives and offers a roadmap for achieving them
  • ensuring everyone in the organization is aligned.
  • Determines Direction: Decisions shape the organization's goals, strategies, and
  • actions, ensuring alignment with its vision and mission.
  • Number of Subordinates
  • o Wide Span of Control: A manager oversees a large number of employees or
  • subordinates.
  • o Narrow Span of Control: A manager supervises only a few employees or
  • subordinates.
  • Efficient Use of Resources: Organizations allocate and utilize resources—like
  • manpower, money, and materials—in a planned and systematic way. This prevents
  • waste and ensures optimal productivity.
  • Efficient Resource Utilization: Management ensures optimal use of limited
  • resources like manpower, capital, and technology, reducing waste and maximizing
  • output.
questions.final_answer: output

questions.question: Give one example of a management function.
questions.solution_html:
• One example of a management function is planning. Planning involves setting objectives
  • determining the best course of action to achieve those objectives, and allocating resources effectively.
  • Autonomy and Flexibility: Each unit or department has the autonomy to make
  • decisions within its scope, leading to quicker responses and greater adaptability to
  • local or departmental needs.
  • Analyzing the Current Situation: Evaluate the existing conditions, including
  • internal strengths and weaknesses, as well as external opportunities and threats.
  • Uncertainty: Since planning relies on future predictions, unexpected changes in
  • external factors (e.g., market conditions, economic shifts) can render plans
  • ineffective.
  • Reduces Uncertainty: By anticipating potential challenges and devising strategies
  • planning minimizes the risks associated with unforeseen events.
  • Problem-Solving: Effective decision-making addresses challenges, resolves conflicts
  • and navigates uncertainties.
  • Hierarchy Levels
  • o Wide Span of Control: Leads to fewer hierarchical levels, resulting in a
  • flatter organizational structure.
  • o Narrow Span of Control: Leads to more hierarchical levels, creating a taller
  • organizational structure.
  • Achieving Objectives: An organization provides a clear framework for setting and
  • achieving specific goals. It aligns individual efforts with the broader vision and
  • mission, ensuring consistency and direction.
  • Adaptation to Change: With rapid changes in markets, technology, and global
  • trends, management helps organizations stay agile and adapt effectively.
questions.final_answer: trends, management helps organizations stay agile and adapt effectively

questions.question: Give any two differences between management and administration.
questions.solution_html:
• Scope and Focus
  •  Management is primarily focused on executing plans, organizing resources, and ensuring
  • daily operations run smoothly.
  •  Administration is more concerned with formulating policies, setting objectives, and
  • overall decision-making at a higher level.
  • Level of Authority
  •  Management operates at the middle and lower levels, implementing strategies and
  • handling operational tasks.
  •  Administration functions at the top level, dealing with strategic planning and policy
  • formulation.
  • Identifying Alternatives: Develop various courses of action or strategies that could
  • help achieve the objectives.
  • Rigidity: Overemphasis on following plans can reduce flexibility and hinder the
  • ability to adapt to new situations.
  • Improves Efficiency: Planning helps allocate resources—time, money, and
  • manpower—more effectively, reducing waste and duplication of efforts.
  • Resource Optimization: It ensures the best use of resources like time, money, and
  • personnel, avoiding waste and maximizing productivity.
  • Manager‟s Attention
  • o Wide Span of Control: Managers may find it challenging to give individual
  • attention to all subordinates.
  • o Narrow Span of Control: Managers can provide closer supervision and
  • personalized guidance.
  • Facilitates Coordination: By assigning roles and responsibilities, organizations
  • ensure that all parts work in harmony. This coordination minimizes duplication of
  • efforts and promotes teamwork.
  • Goal Achievement: It aligns individual efforts with organizational objectives
  • ensuring that everyone works toward the same vision.
questions.final_answer: ensuring that everyone works toward the same vision

questions.question: Define Fayol's principle of 'Division of Work'.
questions.solution_html:
• enri Fayol's principle of 'Division of Work' emphasizes that work should be divided among
  • individuals and teams based on their skills, expertise, and specialization. This specialization
  • allows each person to focus on a specific task, leading to greater efficiency, improved quality
  • and higher productivity
  • Evaluating Alternatives: Assess each alternative based on factors such as feasibility
  • costs, benefits, and risks.
  • Costly Process: Developing and implementing plans may involve considerable
  • financial and human resources.
  • Facilitates Decision-Making: With clear plans, managers can make informed
  • decisions and act with confidence.
  • Cost
  • o Wide Span of Control: Reduces costs due to fewer managers.
  • o Narrow Span of Control: Increases costs due to the need for more managers.
  • Encourages Specialization: Through structured divisions of labor, organizations
  • allow individuals to focus on their areas of expertise. This leads to higher quality
  • work and efficiency.
  • Problem-Solving: Managers identify challenges and develop innovative solutions to
  • overcome them, maintaining smooth operations.
questions.final_answer: overcome them, maintaining smooth operations

questions.question: What is a line and staff organization?
questions.solution_html:
• A line and staff organization is a type of organizational structure that combines the traditional line
  • organization (direct authority and hierarchical structure) with the addition of staff specialists who
  • provide advice, support, and expertise.
  • Adaptability to Change: A well-organized structure can quickly adapt to changes in
  • the external environment, such as market trends, competition, or technological
  • advancements.
  • Motivating Employees: By fostering a positive work environment and recognizing
  • achievements, management keeps employees motivated and productive.
questions.final_answer: achievements, management keeps employees motivated and productive

questions.question: Who typically makes strategic decisions in an organization?
questions.solution_html:
• trategic decisions are typically made by the top-level management of an organization. This includes
  • executives such as the board of directors, CEOs, managing directors, and senior leadership
  • teams. These individuals focus on long-term planning and shaping the organization's overall
  • direction, goals, and policies
  • Decision-Making: Organizations create a hierarchy and define authority levels
  • making the decision-making process more systematic and effective.
  • Strategic Planning: Effective management involves planning for long-term success
  • and tackling competition through well-defined strategies.
questions.final_answer: and tackling competition through well-defined strategies

questions.question: Name one key skill required for effective management.
questions.solution_html:
• One essential skill for effective management is communication. Strong communication ensures that
  • managers can convey ideas, expectations, and goals clearly to their team, foster collaboration, resolve
  • conflicts, and build relationships. It's the backbone of successful leadership, enabling both strategic
  • planning and daily operations to run smoothly.
  • Enhances Communication: Proper organizational structures ensure smooth and clear
  • communication between various levels, departments, and teams.
  • Building Competitive Advantage: Strong management helps organizations innovate
  • differentiate themselves, and maintain their edge in the market.
questions.final_answer: differentiate themselves, and maintain their edge in the market
